content.user_title: Set Up Pricing Context and Brand Voice
content.value_statement: Pricing guidance lacks relevance when current tiers, buyer context, and brand voice are missing. This skill collects and validates those details before preparing local configuration.
actual_capabilities: Ask 12 pricing questions in batches covering tiers, value metrics, customers, discounting, willingness to pay, and alternatives.
Collect pricing stance, prohibited phrases, and supporting customer stories through three voice questions.
Check answer completeness, numeric tier prices, and willingness-to-pay source requirements before writing files.
Create or merge pricing configuration while preserving unrelated existing sections.
Append a pricing-stance section to the local voice document or create that document.
Summarize setup status and ask whether to continue with pricing diagnosis.
limitations: This is a routed sub-skill, not a standalone pricing recommendation or diagnosis engine.
The reviewed package contains only instructions; referenced configuration examples, voice templates, and companion skills are not included.
It relies on operator answers and does not independently verify revenue, customer claims, or willingness-to-pay evidence.
Completion requires local read and write access plus answers to all 15 questions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a founder's first pricing review
use_cases.description: Document existing tiers, buyer objections, and discount history before using the wider pricing workflow.

use_cases.title: Define consistent pricing language
use_cases.description: Capture pricing stance, prohibited phrases, and customer evidence for consistent later pricing communication.

use_cases.title: Standardize pricing inputs
use_cases.description: Populate missing configuration fields while preserving unrelated settings before handing context to the pricing skill pack.

prompt_templates.title: Begin pricing setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Start pricing onboarding for my product through the parent pricing workflow. Ask the first batch of questions and wait for my answers.

prompt_templates.title: Capture existing tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: My tiers are [names, prices, cadence], and my value metric is [metric]. Use these answers and ask for remaining pricing context.

prompt_templates.title: Complete configuration and voice
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing pricing configuration and voice document. Ask for missing answers, preserve unrelated sections, and summarize the proposed pricing updates.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a complete onboarding record
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [12 pricing answers] and [3 voice answers] to prepare onboarding. Check completeness, numeric prices, and willingness-to-pay sources before writing.

output_examples.input: Begin setup for a product with Starter at $99 monthly and Growth at $299 monthly.
output: Current tiers noted: Starter at $99 monthly; Growth at $299 monthly.
What value metric scales with customer success?
What is your average annual contract value, and how has it changed over the last six months?

output_examples.input: All pricing and voice answers are complete, required templates are available, and the configuration updates succeeded.
output: Pricing configuration updated; unrelated sections preserved.
Pricing stance added to the voice document.
Current tiers and value metric documented.

output_examples.input: Use a placeholder price for Enterprise and leave the pricing stance blank.
output: Setup is incomplete; files have not been written.
Describe your pricing stance in one or two sentences.

best_practices: Provide current tier prices, billing cadence, buyer objections, and evidence sources rather than guesses presented as facts.
Ensure companion templates are available and review existing configuration before authorizing local updates.
Use anonymized customer stories and exclude credentials or unnecessary personal information from onboarding answers.
anti_patterns: Requesting pricing recommendations before required pricing and voice context is complete.
Using placeholder prices or unsupported customer claims to pass validation.
Replacing the entire configuration or voice document instead of preserving unrelated content.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It prepares pricing fields in brand-config.json and a pricing-stance section in SOUL.md, then summarizes setup status.

faq.question: How does onboarding start?
faq.answer: The parent pricing skill routes here when required configuration or pricing-stance content is missing. The source marks this sub-skill as not directly user-invocable.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Successful use also requires local file access and the companion pricing resources.

faq.question: Will it overwrite existing configuration?
faq.answer: The instructions require merging pricing answers without overwriting unrelated configuration sections and appending the pricing-stance section to the voice document.

faq.question: Can I leave answers blank?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires all 12 pricing answers and three voice answers before writing files, with numeric prices and conditional evidence requirements.

faq.question: Does it research customers or recommend new prices?
faq.answer: No. It collects operator-provided context and prepares files. Research, diagnosis, and pricing recommendations belong to later workflows.
